title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning to improve queueing fairness and starvation prevention (timeouts & backpressure)
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: production traffic patterns continue to show occasional starvation of low-latency requests when long-running, high-token-generation jobs enter the continuous batcher. This causes P50/P95/P99 skew for small requests and increases customer support noise for interactive endpoints. The goal of this PR is to adjust the continuous batching scheduler to reduce queueing unfairness, prevent starvation of high-priority/small requests, and add configurable timeouts and backpressure signals so the serving runtime can make safer routing decisions.

Changes in this PR: checklist: - [x] introduce priority-aware queue buckets with aging to avoid indefinite starvation - [x] add per-request maximum queue timeout and early-preempt logic to release requests from long waiting queues - [x] implement adaptive batch_window gating: shrink window when high queue latency detected - [x] expose new scheduler metrics (queue_wait_seconds, preempt_count, bucket_size_by_priority) - [x] add integration tests that simulate mixed short/long workloads and verify fairness invariants - [x] add a small e2e perf benchmark and dashboard links in the console notes

Implementation notes: scheduler now tracks requests in three soft-priority buckets (interactive, standard, background). Each queued request gets an insertion timestamp and a priority score that decays with time (aging_factor). The scheduler periodically scans buckets and will preempt a request from a low-priority bucket if a higher-priority request has waited longer than the configured max_queue_time_ms. To avoid oscillation we introduce a min_hold_time for batches and an adaptive backoff that temporarily reduces the effective batch_window_ms when average queue waiting latency exceeds the target SLO. The change is confined to continuous_batcher/* scheduler files and a small runtime hook exposed to the router for backpressure signals.

Testing and validation: unit tests cover priority aging and timeout edge cases; integration (simulated) tests run mixed traffic profiles with synthetic long and short requests; a small perf runner was added to perf-canary that shows 35% reduction in P95 latency for interactive requests at 90th percentile load while keeping aggregate throughput within 3% of baseline. CI: build and unit tests pass; integration job flaked once and was re-run and passed.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged under 'scheduler.priority_fairness_v1' and off by default for Dedicated clusters. Gradual rollout to hosted in controlled rings with canaries and alerting on preempt_count and queue_wait_seconds spikes.

Related: Linear ENG-8742, ENG-9011; incident SUP-453 (customer report for chat latency).

release_notes: Improve continuous batcher fairness: priority buckets, aging-based preemption, per-request queue timeouts, adaptive batch window gating, and new observability metrics. Reduces interactive P95 latency under mixed workloads.
performance_summary: Synthetic mixed-workload runs show interactive request P95 reduced by ~35% at 90% load, P99 reduced by ~20%; overall throughput change within +/-3%. CPU/GPU utilization patterns unchanged. Memory overhead for queue metadata ~1.8MB per shard.
benchmark_results: baseline: interactive P95 = 120ms, P99 = 240ms at target load
with-pr: interactive P95 = 78ms, P99 = 192ms at target load
throughput baseline: 1000 reqs/s, with-pr: 980 reqs/s (2% drop)
notes_for_ops: Feature gated. If enabling in production, monitor metrics: queue_wait_seconds, preempt_count, bucket_size_by_priority, and request_retries. If preempt_count spikes unexpectedly, roll back feature flag and open an incident with tracing payloads.

// continuous_batcher/scheduler.cpp - key preemption check:
if (high_pri_wait > cfg.max_queue_time_ms && low_pri_bucket.size() > 0) { preemptFrom(low_pri_bucket); }

// config.yaml new knobs:
scheduler:
  priority_fairness_v1: true
  max_queue_time_ms: 200
  aging_factor: 0.75
  min_hold_time_ms: 8
  adaptive_batch_window: true
